title: Real Metal
meta_description: Real Metal is an AI-generated Diesel jewellery campaign staged at the gate of Diesel-Land, arguing that a label cannot certify a person but attitude can.
deck: A Diesel jewellery campaign built against the shortcut branded clothing sells: buy the label, become real. The argument here runs the other way. You do not have to wear Diesel to be real — you are real, so you are Diesel.

proof.title: A gate that can only scan metal.
proof.note: Diesel-Land screens everyone at the door, and the detector reads exactly one thing: hardware. It has nothing to say about how a person carries it, which is the only part that decides whether they belong.

shots.alt: Overhead security-camera frame of a woman in denim looking up at an illuminated DIESEL-LAND sign above a metal detector, with REC and CAM 84 overlaid on the image.
shots.caption: Cam 84 / entry

shots.alt: The same overhead camera angle as two men pass through the DIESEL-LAND gate, one pointing at the lens, the frame timestamped 2026-04-27.
shots.caption: Cam 84 / gate

proof.caption: Nobody in frame is waiting to be approved. They look up at the sign, point back at the lens, and wear the metal as though the gate were the thing being inspected.

acts.title: Real metal, real attitude.
acts.note: Three frames, one argument. The gate measures the metal; the people supply everything the metal cannot.

items.title: Diesel-Land
items.copy: The brand as a theme park, borrowing the toy-shop register Diesel has played in before. Admission looks like something you could buy.

items.title: The gate
items.copy: A metal detector under the sign, counting chains and buckles and learning nothing at all about the person wearing them.

items.title: The verdict
items.copy: The question is not whether the metal is real, but whether the attitude is. Only one of the two sets off the machine.

pipeline.title: Pipeline.
pipeline.note: Generated end to end for the Runway AI Film Festival 2026. The campaign has no licence and no photographer, and still reads as unmistakably Diesel — which is the same argument the images are making about people.

items.label: Board
items.copy: Concept and shot order fixed before a single frame was generated: one camera, one gate, one argument.

items.label: Generate
items.copy: Character, wardrobe, and set continuity carried across every camera position.

items.label: Grade
items.copy: A desaturated concrete palette, so the red sign and the chrome are the only colour left.

items.label: Frame
items.copy: The CCTV overlay applied last — camera number, timestamp, recording state — so the jewellery reads as evidence rather than product.
